references.text: Jesus answers this question immediately in the next verse: "What is impossible with man is possible with God" ([ref:Luk 18:27|Luke 18:27]). Salvation is God's work, not man's.
The parallel passage in Matthew where the disciples ask the same question: "Who then can be saved?" and Jesus answers that for God all things are possible ([ref:Matt 19:25-26|Matthew 19:25-26]).
The parallel passage in Mark where those who heard this were even more amazed and asked one another, "Who then can be saved?" ([ref:Mark 10:26-27|Mark 10:26-27]).
The Lord's question to Abraham: "Is anything too hard for the Lord?" ([ref:1 Mos 18:14|Genesis 18:14]). What is impossible for humans to achieve—salvation—is possible with God.
Job acknowledges that nothing is impossible for God: "I know that you can do all things" ([ref:Job 42:2|Job 42:2]). This supports the answer Jesus gives to the question of who can be saved.
Jeremiah's confession: "Nothing is too hard for you" ([ref:Jer 32:17|Jeremiah 32:17]). God's omnipotence makes salvation possible even though it is impossible for humans.
The Lord says through Zechariah: "If this is too hard in the eyes of this people, will it also be too hard in my eyes?" ([ref:Sak 8:6|Zechariah 8:6]). God's power surpasses human limitations.

Paul emphasizes that salvation is God's gift, not from works: "For by grace you have been saved through faith. It is not your own doing; it is the gift of God" ([ref:Ef 2:8-9|Ephesians 2:8-9]). The answer to the question of who can be saved is that salvation comes from God alone.
"Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved" ([ref:Rom 10:13|Romans 10:13]). Salvation is available to all through God's grace, even though it seems impossible by human standards.
